records.name: Early blight
symptoms: Spots started on older lower leaves
distinguishingSymptoms: Spots started on older lower leaves
competingSymptoms: Small round spots with pale centers and dark specks
records.diagnostics: Check older leaves for brown spots with rings. Inspect stems and fruit near the stalk.
records.prevention: Rotate away from tomato and potato, mulch and water at the soil surface.
records.management: Keep leaves dry where possible and ask a crop clinic to check fresh spots.
records.recovery: Inspect newer leaves for new spots and compare with older photos.
records.conditions: Check crop stage and how the damage started and changed.
records.causes: Early blight
records.severity: Check the field to find how much of the crop is affected.
records.sourceOrganization: University of Minnesota Extension
records.geographicApplicability: Use with local field advice
records.evidenceLimitations: Check the crop in the field. Similar signs can have several causes.

records.name: Bacterial wilt
records.sourceOrganization: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University
records.diagnostics: Rapid wilting needs expert stem/root examination and pathogen testing; Fusarium and moisture stress are alternatives.
records.conditions: Record soil moisture, drainage, planting history and the speed of wilting.
records.prevention: Discuss locally suitable rotations and healthy planting material with extension staff.
records.management: Confirm the cause before treatment; symptom agreement does not establish bacterial infection.
records.causes: Possible pathogen or pest; competing abiotic causes remain possible.
records.severity: Severity requires field inspection; matching symptoms are not confirmation.
records.geographicApplicability: Preliminary differential recognition; locally qualified review required
records.evidenceLimitations: Symptom agreement is unconfirmed and uncalibrated. Regional prevalence, treatment validity and diagnostic performance have not been validated.

records.name: Powdery mildew
records.sourceOrganization: University of California IPM
records.diagnostics: Inspect both leaf surfaces and obtain specialist identification of powdery growth; residue and other leaf disorders can resemble mildew.
records.conditions: Temperature, humidity and canopy conditions can support investigation but do not confirm disease.
records.prevention: Inspect leaves regularly and obtain locally applicable canopy management advice.
records.management: Source supports differential recognition; California pesticide guidance is not an India-registered product recommendation.

records.evidenceLimitations: Symptom agreement is unconfirmed and uncalibrated. Regional prevalence, treatment validity and diagnostic performance have not been validated.

distinguishingSymptoms: Pointed spots with gray centers and brown edges
competingSymptoms: Long yellow streaks from leaf tips with wavy edges
records.diagnostics: Check for spots with pointed ends and pale middles. Look at the neck below the grain head too.
records.prevention: Choose locally recommended resistant seed and avoid excess nitrogen.
records.management: Ask an adviser to examine fresh leaf spots and damaged grain heads.
records.recovery: Mark affected patches and check for fresh spots and neck damage.
records.conditions: Check crop stage and how the damage started and changed.
records.causes: Rice blast
records.severity: Check the field to find how much of the crop is affected.

records.geographicApplicability: Use with local field advice

records.name: Septoria leaf spot
symptoms: Small round spots with pale centers and dark specks
Spots started on older lower leaves
distinguishingSymptoms: Small round spots with pale centers and dark specks
Spots started on older lower leaves
records.diagnostics: Look for many small round spots with pale centers, dark rims and tiny dark specks.
records.prevention: Remove volunteer tomatoes and reduce soil splash with mulch.
records.management: Water at soil level and ask a crop clinic to check a spotted leaf.
records.recovery: Check whether new spots are moving up the plant.
records.conditions: Check crop stage and how the damage started and changed.
records.causes: Septoria leaf spot
records.severity: Check the field to find how much of the crop is affected.
records.sourceOrganization: University of Minnesota Extension
records.geographicApplicability: Use with local field advice
records.evidenceLimitations: Check the crop in the field. Similar signs can have several causes.

records.name: Rice tungro
symptoms: Orange-yellow leaf tips with fewer shoots
distinguishingSymptoms: Orange-yellow leaf tips with fewer shoots
records.diagnostics: Check for orange-yellow tips, short plants and fewer shoots. Nitrogen shortage can also cause yellowing.
records.prevention: Ask local extension about resistant rice varieties and planting dates.
records.management: Request a crop clinic check and inspect for green leafhoppers with an adviser.
records.recovery: Record new affected clumps and compare their shoot counts with healthy clumps.
records.conditions: Check crop stage and how the damage started and changed.
records.causes: Rice tungro
records.severity: Check the field to find how much of the crop is affected.
records.sourceOrganization: IRRI
records.geographicApplicability: Use with local field advice
records.evidenceLimitations: Check the crop in the field. Similar signs can have several causes.

records.name: Brown planthopper damage
symptoms: Brown insects at the base of rice stems
distinguishingSymptoms: Brown insects at the base of rice stems
records.diagnostics: Part the stems and look for insects near the base of plants in and around scorched patches.
records.prevention: Scout stem bases regularly and protect beneficial insects.
records.management: Ask an adviser to identify the insects and assess the patch before spraying.
records.recovery: Compare stem bases at the edge and center of the patch at the next check.
records.conditions: Check crop stage and how the damage started and changed.
records.causes: Brown planthopper damage
records.severity: Check the field to find how much of the crop is affected.
records.sourceOrganization: ICAR-NBAIR
records.geographicApplicability: Use with local field advice
records.evidenceLimitations: Check the crop in the field. Similar signs can have several causes.

records.prevention: Maintain drainage paths and check the root zone before irrigating.
records.management: Check outlets and avoid adding water to saturated soil while seeking field advice.
records.recovery: Track how long soil stays wet and watch for healthy new growth.

records.recovery: Photograph new growth and check if the newest leaves still emerge distorted.
